A harvested nanopub is a CANDIDATE, not a record: bringing it in means adding a claim or draft that cites its IRI in prov:wasDerivedFrom, never copying its assertion.

use_cases.does_not_establish: A resolvable identifier is not a read paper. The whole point of the measured-secondhand provenance kind is that a citation that exists can still be a number quoted from a review rather than read in the source.

use_cases.question: In this area, what is actually settled, what is contested, and what is open?

sequence.why: Claims per domain, how many have mathematics, which assessment types can be ranked.
Status is the settled-versus-open axis for the formalised part: 36 accepted, 13 candidate, 7 proposed, 3 contested, 3 retired across 62 law files.
For the big questions, what is formalisable and what is not, per question, with what this repo already has graded real, adjacent or shape-only.

The unsettled half, stated as first-class records rather than inferred from the absence of a law: each question with its arms, its computed belief proportion and what would settle it, plus the theorems that were attempted and failed.
The 215 enumerated open problems, with category and whether they are quantitative. Unreachable from any tool.

worked_example.what: The honest shape of 'settled' here, counted from the registry rather than claimed.
worked_example.result: 62 law files: 36 accepted, 13 candidate, 7 proposed, 3 contested, 3 retired. Lawset 1.7.0 pins 53 of them. Nothing is deleted: retiring or contesting a law changes its status and its history and never removes its file, so the set of things that were once thought settled is also readable.

use_cases.does_not_establish: 'Accepted' is a statement about review, not truth, and the bootstrap laws carry the approving role 'bootstrap-grandfathered' precisely to say that no individual review was recorded. 'Settled' here means 'nobody in this project has contested it yet'.

use_cases.question: What is the smallest change that makes this design legal?

sequence.why: Identify the binding violations with their inputs, which bounds where a repair could act.

A seeded hill climb over decision variables that rejects any candidate with a new binding violation and reports each rejection with the law. It searches for an OBJECTIVE, not for a minimal change, and cannot report that no repair exists.
Try candidate repairs against an inline copy and read the per-edit verdicts without saving anything.
The actual question: the smallest edit set that clears every binding violation, or a certificate that none exists within the stated ranges.

worked_example.what: Why a naive repair search is dangerous here: edits propagate through STATE by stated rules, so a 'small' edit is not small.
worked_example.command: node sim-engine/cli.mjs organism_edit --target pectoral_fin --param area:planform --op scale --value 1.3
worked_example.result: A fin area scale moves STATE pectoral area and span by partedit's own factor rules; a gill volume change by k moves gill area by k^(2/3); a body length, depth, width or size change moves the body-plan parameters with mass held at CONSTANT DENSITY, which is an assumption stated in the source. A set or add of a fin span or length in metres needs the mesh, so STATE flags that it was NOT updated rather than guessing. Any minimal-repair search has to respect all of that or it will report repairs that do not exist.

use_cases.does_not_establish: A minimal change in parameter space is not a minimal change in biology. The edit that moves one number least may be the one no organism could make, and nothing here models developmental or genetic accessibility of an edit.

grand_questions.name: The genotype-to-phenotype map
grand_questions.question: Given a genome, what phenotype does it produce, and why can we not read one off the other?

statements.claim: If the standard genetic code holds and a claimed phenotypic change requires a stated set of amino-acid substitutions, then the number of nucleotide substitutions required is at least the sum of the codon-space distances, so a claimed substitution count below that is impossible.
statements.settles: Rules out a genotype-to-phenotype story whose mutational budget is arithmetically too small. The code is a finite table, so this is decidable rather than merely provable.

statements.claim: If k substitutions are required, the per-site mutation rate is mu, the population size is M and T generations are available, then the expected waiting time is bounded below, so a claimed trajectory faster than that bound is impossible.
statements.settles: Turns 'is this genotype-to-phenotype route reachable in the time available' into an arithmetic question, once the route's substitution count is defined. The repo's own law note says plainly that it eliminates nothing until that count is defined.

statements.claim: If a pleiotropy graph is stated and a view of it omits a set of nodes, then the view's closure under the part-of and affects relations is determined, so a claim that the view captures a phenotype's determinants either follows or does not.
statements.settles: What a partial map of the genotype-phenotype map is allowed to leave out. This is a statement about what a VIEW may omit, not about development, and the registry says so in the law's own note.

statements.claim: If a trait is additive with stated allele frequencies p_i and effect sizes alpha_i, then the additive genetic variance is the sum of 2 p_i q_i alpha_i squared, so a claimed heritability inconsistent with that sum is impossible under additivity.
statements.settles: The arithmetic half of the missing-heritability problem: whether a reported heritability is even consistent with the reported effect sizes under the model the authors state.

items.what: Whether the map is additive at all, and if not, the structure and dimension of the epistatic interaction.
items.why_not_provable: A proof can only say what follows from an assumed functional form. Which functional form is right is a fact about organisms.
items.measurement: Systematic double- and higher-order mutant panels in one organism, with the same phenotype measured throughout.

items.what: Which loci affect the trait, and with what effect sizes.
items.why_not_provable: No premise set determines the actual architecture of an actual trait; this is the content of every GWAS.
items.measurement: Association studies and, for causality, allele-replacement experiments.

items.what: Whether the trait is a well-defined measurable at all, or an aggregate that different studies operationalise differently.
items.why_not_provable: This is a question about measurement practice, not about a formal system.
items.measurement: Cross-laboratory harmonisation of the phenotype definition before any genetic analysis.

items.what: Whether most variation acts through a small number of core genes or diffusely through nearly all of them (the omnigenic question).
items.why_not_provable: Both pictures are consistent with the same formalism; they differ in what the effect-size distribution actually is.
items.measurement: Effect-size distributions across traits at sufficient sample size, with regulatory and expression data.

grand_questions.name: How a genome specifies a body plan
grand_questions.question: How does a one-dimensional sequence specify a three-dimensional animal, reliably, at the right size, generation after generation?
grand_questions.dispute: Whether patterning is best understood as positional information read from morphogen gradients (Wolpert) or as the output of a dynamical system whose transient behaviour carries the specification (Jaeger and Verd), and separately whether a given gradient is set by free diffusion with degradation or by hindered diffusion through binding.

statements.claim: If a morphogen is produced at a source, diffuses with coefficient D and is degraded first-order with rate k, then at steady state the gradient length is the square root of D over k, so a claimed gradient length inconsistent with the claimed D and k is impossible under this model.
statements.settles: Whether a published gradient length is consistent with the published coefficients, under the stated model. In this repo lambda works out at about 209 micrometres against an independently reported ~200, and that 4.4 per cent agreement is why the two fetched numbers are trusted at all.

statements.claim: If a two-species reaction-diffusion system has stated kinetics and diffusion coefficients, then whether it satisfies the diffusion-driven-instability conditions is determined by those premises alone.
statements.settles: Turing's question exactly: it is a question about the premises, and the inequalities follow from them. Proved here as a candidate law, so it is in no law set and judges no design yet.

statements.claim: If a body plan is given as a part-of graph with levels, then it is a well-formed body plan only if the graph is levels-down, closed, rooted and its taxon data are consistent; and a Boolean check of those conditions implies well-formedness.
statements.settles: That a proposed body plan is a body plan at all. Modest, and the honest version of 'Lean checks the blueprint': it rules out incoherent descriptions, not biologically impossible animals.

statements.claim: If an expansion-repression feedback with stated parameters operates, then the pattern scales with domain size, so a claim that a mechanism without such feedback nevertheless scales does not follow from its stated premises.
statements.settles: Which proposed scaling mechanisms actually imply scaling, separating mechanism from the observation that scaling occurs.

items.what: Whether the actual mechanism is free diffusion with degradation, hindered diffusion through heparan-sulfate binding, cell-lineage specification, or mechanics.
items.why_not_provable: All four are internally consistent models. Which one operates is a fact about tissue.
items.measurement: Single-molecule and FCS measurement of the mobile fraction in the actual tissue at the actual stage, with binding perturbed.

items.what: The actual D and k in the actual tissue at the actual developmental stage.
items.why_not_provable: A proof takes these as inputs. This repo's own numbers are gastrula measurements being used for a 72-hour fin bud, and every scope string says so.
items.measurement: FCS or photoconversion in the fin bud itself, not the gastrula.

items.what: Whether thresholds are read as positional information at all, or whether the cell's state depends on the gradient's history.
items.why_not_provable: This is the Wolpert-versus-dynamic dispute, and it is about what cells do, not about what follows from a model.
items.measurement: Time-resolved single-cell readouts under gradients with the same final value but different histories.

items.what: Why body plans are conserved for hundreds of millions of years and then, rarely, are not.
items.why_not_provable: A historical question about contingent events.
items.measurement: Comparative developmental genetics across the relevant divergences; in part not measurable at all.

grand_questions.name: The major evolutionary transitions
grand_questions.question: Why did replicators become chromosomes, cells become eukaryotes, individuals become societies? What makes a transition in individuality happen, and why so rarely?

statements.claim: If an asexual variant has a twofold reproductive advantage factor and starts at frequency q, then its frequency after n generations is determined, so a claim that sex persists without a compensating benefit of at least that size does not follow.
statements.settles: The arithmetic of the cost of sex, which is the quantitative core of the sex transition. It settles the size of the benefit that any explanation must supply; it does not identify the benefit.

statements.claim: If a transition requires a stated number of substitutions and the population and mutation parameters are stated, then the available time bounds whether it could occur at all.
statements.settles: Whether a proposed transition route is reachable, as a budget question. Our Haldane-cost law does exactly this FROM a named hypothesis, and the registry records that the hypothesis itself has been contested since 1957.

statements.claim: If a multilevel population has stated within- and between-group fitnesses and a stated group structure, then the direction of change in the group-level character follows from the Price partition, so a claimed direction inconsistent with the partition is impossible.
statements.settles: Whether a verbal argument about a transition's direction is an algebraic consequence of its own stated structure. Requires the Price equation, which this repo does not have.

items.what: Which selective force actually drove each transition.
items.why_not_provable: A historical cause, and in several cases the evidence is a single lineage.
items.measurement: Comparative phylogenetics plus experimental evolution of de novo transitions; for the deepest transitions, no measurement exists.

items.what: Whether each transition happened once or repeatedly, and what the ancestral states were.
items.why_not_provable: Facts about a particular history.
items.measurement: Phylogenomics; palaeontology where there is a record.

items.what: Whether sex is maintained by recombination's effect on deleterious mutation load, by host-parasite dynamics, or by something else.
items.why_not_provable: Every candidate benefit is formally capable of exceeding the twofold cost. Which one does is empirical.
items.measurement: Experimental evolution with recombination rate manipulated and load measured directly.

grand_questions.name: Levels of selection and the Price equation
grand_questions.question: When does selection act on the group rather than on the individual, and is the distinction a fact about the world or a choice of bookkeeping?
grand_questions.dispute: Not about the algebra, which is an identity, but about whether the multilevel partition identifies real causes or is one of several equally valid accounting schemes (Okasha; Frank). The persistence of the dispute despite the algebra being settled is itself the evidence that the formal and causal questions have been run together.

statements.claim: If fitness, character and the covariance operator are defined as stated, then the change in mean character equals the covariance of fitness with character over mean fitness, plus the fitness-weighted expectation of within-individual change. This is an identity, not a hypothesis.
statements.settles: Everything about the algebra. The Price equation is fully provable, and once proved, every claimed rearrangement of it is mechanically checkable as following or not following. This is the most Lean-tractable question on this list.

statements.claim: If a population is partitioned into groups as stated, then the multilevel expansion of the Price equation into between-group and within-group terms follows; and a claim that group selection is REQUIRED to explain a given change is an additional causal assertion, not an algebraic consequence of the partition.
statements.settles: Exactly where the formal content stops and the causal reading begins. A proof of this would let a reviewer see, mechanically, which steps of a multilevel-selection argument are algebra and which are interpretation.

statements.claim: If a character has zero between-group covariance with fitness under a stated partition, then the between-group term vanishes, so a claimed group-level effect under that partition does not follow.
statements.settles: A decidable elimination for a stated dataset and partition, in the shape this repo already uses for its other laws.

items.what: Whether the between-group covariance is non-zero in any particular real population.
items.why_not_provable: The identity holds whatever the numbers are; the numbers are measurements.
items.measurement: Fitness and character measured at both levels in a structured population, with group membership defined before the analysis.

items.what: Whether the multilevel partition picks out causes or is one valid bookkeeping among several.
items.why_not_provable: This is a question about what causation is, not about what follows from the definitions. Formalisation would sharpen it and could not answer it.
items.measurement: Not measurable. Settled, if at all, by intervention experiments that change group structure while holding individual properties fixed.

items.what: Which level of description is most predictive in practice.
items.why_not_provable: Predictive performance is an empirical property of a model applied to data.
items.measurement: Out-of-sample prediction contests between individual-level and multilevel models on the same populations.

grand_questions.name: Hamilton's rule and its generality
grand_questions.question: Does relatedness times benefit exceeding cost explain altruism in general, or only under assumptions that rarely hold?
grand_questions.dispute: Nowak, Tarnita and Wilson 2010 argued that inclusive-fitness theory has been of little explanatory value; 137 authors replied in Abbot et al. 2011; Gardner, West and Wild 2011 defended the rule's generality formally; Birch, and Birch and Okasha, argue that the dispute turns on the difference between a general form that is a tautologous rearrangement and a restricted form with substantive premises. Fifteen years of it, and the formal half has never been mechanically settled.

statements.claim: If the change in mean breeding value takes the Price form dp = k(rb - c) with k > 0 and 0 <= r <= 1, where b and c are the partial regressions of fitness on the partner's and the actor's genotype, then the trait increases if and only if c < rb.
statements.settles: That the GENERAL form is a theorem under those definitions, and therefore has no empirical content on its own: it cannot be refuted by any data until the coefficients are measured. Proved here as a candidate law. Read the premise carefully: the Price form is a NAMED HYPOTHESIS of this law, not something derived from a proved Price identity, so what is settled is the biconditional and not the Price form itself. Deriving that premise is what the missing Price module would do.

statements.claim: If interactions are pairwise, selection is weak, and fitness effects are additive, then rb greater than c with r the pedigree coefficient of relatedness implies the altruistic allele increases.
statements.settles: That the RESTRICTED form is a substantive theorem whose premises can fail. Its premises become visible and checkable, which is what the dispute needs.

statements.claim: There exists a model with stated non-additive fitness effects, satisfying pairwise interaction and pedigree relatedness, in which rb exceeds c and the allele nevertheless decreases.
statements.settles: That the restricted form does NOT follow without additivity. This is a counter-model, not a failed proof attempt, and it is the formal content of one side of the dispute. No tool here can produce or certify one.

items.why_not_provable: A measurement about pedigrees and population structure.
items.measurement: Genotyping of colonies and estimation of within-colony relatedness, in the clades where eusociality originated.

items.why_not_provable: A question about scientific practice; both are formally valid if the general forms are theorems.

grand_questions.name: Fisher's fundamental theorem and its interpretation
grand_questions.question: Does natural selection increase mean fitness at a rate equal to the additive genetic variance in fitness, and if so, under what conditions and in what sense?
grand_questions.dispute: Fisher 1930 stated it as having 'the supreme position among the biological sciences'; Price 1972 made clear it concerns only the partial change due to allele-frequency change in a constant environment; Ewens 1989 and Ewens and Lessard 2015 gave the standard modern reading; Grafen 2018 offered a third; Basener and Sanford 2018 claimed it fails with mutation and Hancock and Cardinale 2024 replied directly. Every one of those positions is a claim about which premises the theorem needs, which is why this question's formalisable core is unusually large.

statements.claim: If a haploid population has frequency vector p and constant fitnesses w, then after selection the change in mean fitness equals the variance of w under p divided by the mean of w.
statements.settles: The theorem under its narrowest honest reading. It is proved here, and what it establishes is a consequence of constant fitnesses and a finite type, not a fact about any population.

statements.claim: Under the same premises, mean fitness is non-decreasing; and therefore a claimed DECLINE in mean fitness under constant fitnesses and no mutation is impossible.
statements.settles: The elimination form: a claimed trajectory of mean fitness that falls, with the premises stated, is ruled out. The repo proves the elimination separately from the equality.

statements.claim: If the additive genetic variance in fitness is zero, then the change in mean fitness is zero, so a claimed change under zero variance is impossible.
statements.settles: The degenerate case, proved separately, which is where overstated readings of the theorem break first.

statements.claim: If mutation is added with a stated rate and a stated effect distribution, then the change in mean fitness is NOT in general equal to the additive variance over the mean, and the conditions under which the equality survives are determined.
statements.settles: The Basener-Sanford dispute's formal half: whether the theorem's scope extends to mutation-selection balance. It is a question about premises, and a formalisation would make each side's premises explicit instead of arguable.

items.what: Whether mean fitness actually increases in any real population over any real interval.
items.why_not_provable: The theorem is silent on this, and the commonest misreading of it is to treat the proof as the answer.
items.measurement: Longitudinal fitness measurement in a population with a stable definition of fitness, which is itself contested.

items.what: Whether the environment is constant, which the narrow form requires and which is almost never true.
items.why_not_provable: An empirical property of the population's circumstances.
items.measurement: Measurement of fitness-relevant environmental variation over the same interval as the fitness measurement.

items.what: Whether the additive approximation to the genetic variance is adequate for the trait in question.
items.why_not_provable: Depends on the actual genetic architecture.
items.measurement: Variance decomposition from a breeding design or a mutant panel.

items.what: What the actual mutation rate and effect distribution are, which decides whether the mutation-selection extension matters in practice.
items.why_not_provable: Both are measurements of a particular organism in a particular environment.
items.measurement: Mutation-accumulation lines with fitness assayed.

grand_questions.name: The error threshold and Eigen's paradox
grand_questions.question: A replicator needs an accurate copying machine, and an accurate copying machine needs a long genome, which needs accurate copying. How did the first one get started?

statements.claim: If per-base copying fidelity is q, genome length is L and the master sequence's selective superiority is sigma, then the master sequence is maintained only if q to the power L exceeds one over sigma; equivalently L is less than the natural log of sigma over one minus q.
statements.settles: Whether a claimed prebiotic genome length is compatible with a claimed fidelity. This is an inequality between stated quantities, so it is fully provable, and it eliminates in exactly the shape this repo's other laws do.

statements.claim: If a hypercycle of n stated catalytic couplings is posited, then the total information maintained follows from the per-member thresholds, so a claimed total exceeding their sum does not follow.
statements.settles: Whether a proposed escape from the paradox actually escapes it, given its own stated structure.

statements.claim: If the fitness landscape contains lethal mutants in stated proportion, then the threshold's location changes in a determined direction, so a claim that the threshold disappears under lethality does not follow from lethality alone.

grand_questions.name: Metabolic scaling and Kleiber's law
grand_questions.question: Why does metabolic rate scale with body mass to a power near three-quarters rather than two-thirds, and is there a single exponent at all?
grand_questions.dispute: West, Brown and Enquist 1997 derive 3/4 from a space-filling fractal network; Dodds, Rothman and Weitz 2001 argue 2/3 is the null hypothesis and 3/4 is not established; Kolokotrones et al. 2010 find the relation is curved, so no single exponent exists; White, Blackburn and Seymour 2009 find mammalian data support neither. Two separable disputes have been run together: whether the derivation follows from its premises, and what the exponent is.

statements.claim: If a distribution network is space-filling, has area-preserving branching and size-invariant terminal units, then the exponent relating throughput to volume is determined, so a claimed exponent inconsistent with those premises does not follow from them.
statements.settles: Whether the famous derivation is valid, separately from whether its premises describe real vasculature. The derivation's validity is a mathematical question nobody has mechanically checked, and asymmetric branching is already flagged as an open question in this repo's own enumeration.

statements.claim: If a family of organisms grows isometrically by linear factor k, then mass scales as k cubed while cross-sectional area and breaking load scale as k squared, so a claimed load-bearing performance at a larger size is impossible beyond a determined limit.
statements.settles: The square-cube half of the problem, which is the part that actually eliminates designs. Proved here, for any isometric family.

statements.claim: If the measured mass exponent for a clade lies in a stated band, then a claimed weight ratio outside the band implied by that exponent is ruled out.
statements.settles: Elimination against a measured band rather than against a theoretical exponent. This is an EMPIRICAL law here, labelled as such, and the repo's E1 proves that a within-species area exponent is not 2, so the theorem and the measurement are recorded as disagreeing.

statements.claim: If a stated aerobic supply chain delivers at most a stated rate, then a claimed sustained power demand above it is impossible.
statements.settles: The metabolic budget as an elimination, from the Fick principle as a named hypothesis. Proved here, and scoped so that it bounds sustained aerobic demand and explicitly not unpowered descent or burst effort.

items.what: What the exponent is, and whether a single exponent is the right model at all.
items.why_not_provable: Kolokotrones et al. report curvature, which means the question 'what is the exponent' may be malformed. No proof settles which functional form fits.
items.measurement: Basal metabolic rate against mass across many species with phylogenetic correction, over enough mass range to detect curvature.

items.what: Whether real vascular networks satisfy space-filling, area-preserving branching and invariant terminal units.
items.why_not_provable: These are anatomical facts.
items.measurement: Quantitative vascular morphometry, including whether branching is asymmetric.

items.what: Whether organisms grow isometrically, which every theorem above assumes.
items.why_not_provable: An empirical fact, and this repo's own E1 proves a within-species area exponent is not 2, so the answer is already known to be no.
items.measurement: Ontogenetic series with area and mass measured at several sizes.

grand_questions.name: The origin of the genetic code
grand_questions.question: Why does this code, and not one of the million alternatives, map 64 codons onto 20 amino acids?

statements.claim: If the standard code holds, then the minimum number of nucleotide substitutions between the codon sets of two amino acids is a determined number, and a claimed substitution path shorter than it is impossible.
statements.settles: Combinatorial facts about the code, by kernel decision over a finite table rather than by argument. Phenylalanine to leucine is one substitution; methionine to tryptophan is two; this repo proves both.

statements.claim: If an objective function over codon assignments is stated and the space of alternative codes is stated, then whether the standard code is optimal within that space is determined.
statements.settles: The 'one in a million' style of claim, as a decidable question for each stated objective and each stated space. It does NOT settle whether the objective is the one selection acted on, which is the whole difficulty.

items.what: Why the code is as it is: frozen accident, stereochemical affinity, coevolution with biosynthesis, or error minimisation.
items.why_not_provable: A historical and chemical question. An optimality proof within a stated space is consistent with all four accounts.

gaps.name: lean_counter_model
gaps.need: Prove that a claimed implication does NOT hold in general, by constructing and kernel-checking a model that satisfies the premises and falsifies the conclusion.
gaps.signature: lean_counter_model({premises, conclusion} | {law_id, drop_hypothesis}) -> {status: 'counter-model'|'none-found'|'inconsistent-premises', witness_lean, instance_values, checked, envelope}

buildable.why: The registry already builds the mirror-image object: a non-vacuity witness showing the hypotheses CAN be satisfied, with bridges proved in Witnesses.lean. A counter-model is a witness plus a proof that the conclusion fails on it, and the same build and checking machinery applies.

gaps.risk: A counter-model is relative to the formalisation, so it can refute a formalisation nobody held. It must return the full instance values and the Lean source, so a reader can check that the model is not a degenerate case the original author would have excluded.

gaps.name: premise_check
gaps.need: Given a stated conclusion and stated premises, return whether the conclusion is derivable, not derivable, or derivable only with a named additional premise.
gaps.signature: premise_check({premises: [...], conclusion, idiom?}) -> {verdict: 'derivable'|'not-derivable'|'needs-premise', formalisation, missing_premise?, lean_source, proof_or_gap, envelope}

buildable.why: Needs premise_extract for its input and automated proof search for its output. Lean will say whether a proof the tool wrote compiles; it will not find the proof, and a failed search is not a non-derivation.

gaps.risk: Confusing 'I could not find a proof' with 'it does not follow'. Those are different claims and only the second is interesting, which is why lean_counter_model is a separate gap rather than part of this one. A tool that conflated them would systematically accuse correct papers of error.

gaps.need: One table of every number behind an answer, with its provenance kind and source, across a whole tool sequence or a whole corpus, rather than one envelope at a time.
gaps.signature: provenance_audit({envelopes: [...]} | {organism_id, scenario} | {corpus: 'claims'|'laws'|'state'}) -> {rows: [{quantity, value, kind, source, used_by}], counts_by_kind, weakest_input, blocking: [...], envelope}

buildable.why: Every tool here already returns {result, provenance, scope, weakest_input, counts} and the envelope throws without a scope string. The tool is an aggregator over a shape that is already enforced at runtime, with an unknown kind already rejected so a typo cannot slip through.

gaps.risk: Aggregation can launder a weak input: a table of fifty rows with one 'calibrated' entry reads as well-sourced. The tool must surface the weakest kind and the blocking rows first, and a calibrated quantity can never be cited as a result, which the output must repeat rather than assume.

gaps.name: premise_extract
gaps.need: Read the premises out of a claim's or a paper's prose, as a structured list of named hypotheses with their sources, so there is something to formalise and compare against.
gaps.signature: premise_extract({text | claim_id}) -> {premises: [{name, statement, quantities, source, confidence, span}], conclusion, unparsed_spans, envelope}

buildable.why: The assumptions in this corpus are free text inside delphi:context, and the existing typing is first-match-wins regex whose precision has not been measured. Reliable premise extraction is a research-grade language task, and the honest version of this tool reports what it could NOT parse, like parse_design_text does.
needs_data: a hand-annotated set of claims with their premises marked, to measure precision against

gaps.risk: The worst failure in the map. A plausible but wrong premise list makes every downstream check wrong while looking rigorous, and the reviewer use case would then produce confident verdicts about manuscripts. It must follow parse_design_text's rule of reporting every span it could not read, and must never silently complete a premise set.

gaps.name: evidence_value
gaps.need: For a claim, which measurement would move its belief most, and by how much on each outcome. lean_open_question states what would settle one of this project's seven open questions and whether that is feasible; this would compute the movement, for any claim in the 941-record corpus, by simulating the evidence item.
gaps.signature: evidence_value({claim_id, candidates?: [{source_class, side}]}) -> {current: {belief, E, R, items}, candidates: [{source_class, belief_if_supports, belief_if_refutes, crosses_queue_threshold, independent_of_existing}], envelope}

buildable.why: belief.mjs already computes belief from a list of evidence items with source-class deduplication. Adding a hypothetical item and recomputing is a few lines; the deduplication rule means the tool correctly reports zero movement for a duplicate source, which is the interesting case.

gaps.risk: A number like 'this measurement moves belief by 0.3' invites being read as a decision-theoretic value of information. The parameters are hand-set and were never fitted to a curated corpus, so the number is a property of this scorer and nothing else. It must be returned with the parameter version attached.

gaps.name: literature_evidence_add
gaps.need: Resolve a DOI or PMID against Europe PMC or Crossref, confirm the record exists, and attach it as an evidence item with its source class.
gaps.signature: literature_evidence_add({claim_id, identifier, side: 'supports'|'refutes', quoted_sentence}) -> {resolved: {ref, doi, pmid, title, year, fetched_at}, evidence_item, belief_before, belief_after, duplicate_of?, envelope}

buildable.why: Both endpoints are public, unauthenticated and already the ones this project uses for citations, and the pipeline already has a committed cache pattern so reruns and CI stay offline. The belief recomputation is a pure function call.

gaps.risk: A resolvable identifier is not a read paper. The tool must not let a fetched title stand in for the quoted sentence, and the provenance kind for a number taken from such a record is 'measured-secondhand' at best. Writing the cache on a hosted server would also mean making outbound calls for anonymous clients, which leanbio_ground already forbids in hosted mode.

gaps.name: open_questions_list
gaps.need: Serve the 215-problem literature enumeration in open-problems/, which exists as files and is reachable from no tool. The open-questions thread's lean_open_questions serves a DIFFERENT and narrower thing well: this project's own first-class open questions (7 questions with Lean-formalised arms and computed belief proportions, 4 failed theorems, 11 requirements), all specific to this project's organisms and laws. The literature enumeration behind them is still unserved.
gaps.signature: open_questions_list({category?, quantitative?, has_candidates?, text?, limit}) -> {total, items: [{id, statement, source, category, quantitative, candidates: [{id, commitment, checkable_against, origin, uses_illustrative_values}]}], sources, envelope}

buildable.why: Nothing to build but the serving layer: 215 problems with sources, 80 candidates for 47 eligible problems, 44 carrying checkable_against, and a formal translation set already written by the Lean thread. The lowest-effort, highest-breadth gap in this list, and the open-questions registry gives it a shape to follow.

gaps.risk: A served list looks canonical. SOURCES.md states plainly that no exhaustive list of open problems exists, that the Wikipedia source carries a citations-needed banner, and that coverage is weighted toward evolution and organism design. All three must travel in the envelope. It must also not be confused with lean_open_questions: that tool answers "what has THIS project failed to settle", this one would answer "what does the literature list as open", and conflating them would make a seven-item project backlog look like the state of biology.

gaps.name: minimal_repair
gaps.need: Given a violated design, the smallest edit set that clears every binding violation, or a certificate that none exists within the stated ranges.
gaps.signature: minimal_repair({organism_id, ageDays, conditions, ranges: [{target, param, min, max}], metric: 'edits'|'relative-change'}) -> {status: 'repaired'|'no-repair-in-range'|'irreparable', edits, cleared, still_violated, searched, envelope}

buildable.why: organism_edit already validates targets and returns verdicts, swarm_try_edits already applies edits to an inline copy without saving, and optimize already rejects candidates with new binding violations. What is missing is the minimality objective and the no-repair certificate, not the machinery.

gaps.risk: Edits propagate through STATE by stated rules (a fin area scale moves span, a gill volume change moves area by the two-thirds power, a body size change moves mass at constant density), so a change that is minimal in one parameter is not minimal in the organism. And a minimal change in parameter space may be one no organism could make: nothing here models the developmental or genetic accessibility of an edit, and the output must say so.

gaps.name: teach_claim
gaps.need: One claim or law packaged as a teachable unit: the theorem, its premises with sources, what it does not establish, an in-scope and an out-of-scope example, and a mutant whose proof fails.
gaps.signature: teach_claim({law_id | claim_id, level: 'undergraduate'|'graduate'}) -> {statement_en, premises: [{name, statement, source}], lean_source, does_not_establish, in_scope_example, out_of_scope_example, failing_mutant, envelope}

buildable.why: Every component already exists in a law file: statement_en, hypotheses with sources, scope with taxa and ranges, the non-vacuity witness, and the mutation results recorded by propose.mjs. The work is assembly and choosing the out-of-scope example, which the scope table already determines.

gaps.risk: A teaching package makes a law look settled. The bootstrap laws carry the approving role 'bootstrap-grandfathered', meaning no individual review was recorded, and the does_not_establish field must be mandatory rather than optional or it will be the first thing dropped.

gaps.name: scale_coverage
gaps.need: For a gene, a part or an organism, what is known and what is NOT known at each biological scale, with absence as a first-class answer rather than an empty result.
gaps.signature: scale_coverage({entity, kind: 'gene'|'part'|'organism'|'taxon', scales?}) -> {per_scale: [{scale, known: [{what, source, provenance_kind}], not_in_dataset: [...], never_looked: [...]}], weakest_scale, envelope}

buildable.why: Every input is already in the repo and already read by an existing tool. The work is the join and, harder, deciding the three-way distinction between 'measured and recorded', 'not in this dataset' and 'nobody looked', which has to be derivable from the files rather than asserted.

gaps.risk: An empty row would read as 'science does not know this' when it means 'this repo does not hold it'. The tool must distinguish absence-in-corpus from absence-in-literature in its output shape, not in a footnote, or it will be quoted as the former.

gaps.name: lean_module_genotype_network
gaps.need: Reachability and distance in a stated genotype space, generalising the proved codon-space case to an arbitrary stated mutational neighbourhood.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/GenotypeNetwork.lean with Delphi.GNet.reachable_within, Delphi.GNet.distance_ge and Delphi.GNet.claimed_reachability_rules_out, entering the registry as law_id `genotype-network-reachability`
reads: Mathlib Relation.TransGen as used in lean/Delphi/Blueprint.lean

buildable.why: Both halves exist: a decided finite-graph distance in Genotype.lean and transitive-closure reasoning over a stated graph in Blueprint.lean. The module is their combination over an abstract neighbourhood relation.

gaps.risk: A reachability result is relative to the stated neighbourhood, and real mutational accessibility is measured, not stated. The law must be scoped so that 'unreachable in this stated space' cannot be quoted as 'evolutionarily impossible'. This one module serves three grand questions, which makes it the highest-leverage Lean target after Price.

gaps.name: lean_module_price_equation
gaps.need: The Price equation as a proved identity, with the multilevel partition, so that every argument built on it can be checked as following or not following.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/Price.lean with Delphi.Price.price_identity and Delphi.Price.multilevel_partition, entering the registry as law_id `price-equation` and served by lean_law_get

buildable.why: It is an identity over a finite index type, and the exact machinery is already in Fisher.lean: a frequency vector with IsFreq, a selection operator proved to preserve it, a mean and a variance. No data is needed, because an identity has no empirical premises.

gaps.risk: The Price equation is an identity, so proving it establishes nothing about any population, and the registry class must be `theorem` with a statement_en that says so. The real risk is the opposite of overreach: a proved identity being cited as a result about group selection, which is the confusion the formalisation is supposed to end.

gaps.name: lean_sketch
gaps.need: Turn a typed statement (relation, subject, object, quantities) into a Lean skeleton with named hypotheses, the theorem shape and a witness stub, so a first file is not written from a blank page.
gaps.signature: lean_sketch({claim_id | statement: {relation, subject, object, quantities}}) -> {lean_source, meta_json, hypotheses_needing_sources, witness_stub, next_steps, envelope}
reads: lean/registry/propose.mjs header for the meta.json fields

buildable.why: The relation vocabulary is versioned and small (ScalingLaw, Bound, Equality, Dynamics, Comparative and the INDRA types), and 62 existing law files supply the idioms per relation. A template per relation family covers most of it.

gaps.risk: A skeleton that compiles trivially. The generated statement must be non-vacuous and must fail its own mutants, or the tool manufactures proposals that pass propose.mjs while saying nothing. The stub should refuse to emit a theorem whose hypotheses have no source field.

gaps.name: question_rank
gaps.need: Open questions ordered ACROSS questions by how decisive new evidence would be, rather than by how often they are cited. lean_open_question already gives, per question, what would settle it and whether that is feasible today; nothing ranks questions against each other, and nothing covers the literature enumeration.
gaps.signature: question_rank({field?, category?, limit, measure: 'belief-movement'|'claims-flipped'|'both'}) -> {items: [{question_id, statement, source, expected_belief_movement, claims_that_would_flip, formalisable, inputs_used}], method, envelope}
reads: lean/registry/open-questions/questions/*.json (arms, computed belief proportion, what would settle it)

buildable.why: 215 enumerated problems with sources, 80 formal candidates, and a belief function that is pure and therefore simulable with a hypothetical evidence item added. Nothing has to be fetched.

gaps.risk: A ranked list of research questions looks like a funding recommendation. It ranks movement in OUR hand-set belief function, which is not calibrated to anything, and says nothing about importance, tractability or cost. The output must carry the ranking's inputs so it can be argued with rather than cited.

gaps.name: data_metabolic_rate_mass
gaps.need: Metabolic rate against body mass across species with phylogenetic information, over enough mass range to test for curvature rather than assume an exponent.
gaps.signature: a sourced dataset under sim-engine/params/ or omics/, each row carrying its source, the measurement conditions and its provenance kind, with an empirical band law derived from it
reads: no existing repo file: this is an acquisition

buildable.why: This repo holds length, area, mass and aerobic-budget data. It has nothing on metabolic rate against body mass across species, and no amount of tooling creates it.
needs_data: basal or standard metabolic rate with body mass, per species, with measurement conditions and a phylogeny

gaps.risk: A compiled dataset inherits every compiler's judgement about which measurements are comparable, which is precisely what the curvature dispute turns on. Rows must carry measurement conditions, and any band derived from it must be scoped to the taxa actually in it, as E2 is scoped to one family because it rests on six studies of it. No avian rows: this project holds a clade out as a blind exam.

gaps.name: contradiction_scan
gaps.need: Scan the claim set for pairs whose stated premises or conclusions are jointly inconsistent over the quantities they share.
gaps.signature: contradiction_scan({domain?, min_shared_quantities, prove?}) -> {pairs: [{a, b, shared_quantities, status: 'proved-inconsistent'|'suspected'|'consistent-over-shared', proof?}], scanned, envelope}

buildable.why: The machinery exists for LAWS: shared-scope atoms, a bridge proving the Lean structure equivalent to them, and a proved-contradiction path in propose.mjs. Extending it to claims needs structured premises and shared quantities per claim, which means premise_extract first.

gaps.risk: 'Suspected inconsistent' pairs would be read as proved ones. Only the proved tier means anything, and the suspected tier will be dominated by claims that use the same word for different quantities, which is exactly the failure the shared-scope atoms were introduced to avoid.

gaps.name: adhesion_mechanics
gaps.need: Force, contact and cell-matrix mechanics, and the integrin signalling that would couple them to the morphogen field.
gaps.signature: a tool set implementing the sim-engine contract's names and envelope, supplied by a collaborator's MCP server and swapped in as a configuration change
reads: sim-engine/contract.json for the names and schemas
sim-engine/lib/envelope.mjs for the envelope and provenance kinds

buildable.why: Out of scope here by instruction, and CONTRACT.md names it as the natural module for the collaborator's server. Nothing in this repo models force, contact or adhesion, and no tool here should be read as if it did.
needs_data: adhesion and cell-matrix mechanical parameters for the tissue and stage in question

gaps.risk: The contract is mechanical except in one respect: a tool must not report a number as 'measured' that it did not read in a primary source for the organism in question. A replacement server that labels everything measured satisfies the schema and destroys the contract, and CONTRACT.md says exactly that.

gaps.name: lean_module_hamilton_rule
gaps.need: Both forms of Hamilton's rule: the general form proved from the Price identity, the restricted form proved from pairwise interaction, weak selection and additivity, and a counter-model for the restricted form without additivity.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/Hamilton.lean with Delphi.Hamilton.general_form (from Price), Delphi.Hamilton.restricted_form (from named hypotheses) and Delphi.Hamilton.restricted_fails_without_additivity, entering the registry as two laws plus a counter-model record
reads: lean/registry/lean/Witnesses.lean for the witness and bridge idiom

buildable.why: Depends on the Price module, which does not exist, and on lean_counter_model for its third statement. Nothing about relatedness or social interaction exists in this repo at all today.

gaps.risk: The highest-value and highest-risk item on the list. Formalising both forms would settle which definitions make the rule a theorem; it would settle nothing about whether kin selection explains eusociality, and in a dispute this public the result would certainly be reported as the latter. The statement_en and scope must be written to make that misreading hard, and the empirical remainder must be carried in the law file itself.

gaps.name: lean_module_pattern_scaling
gaps.need: Which stated patterning mechanisms imply that the pattern scales with domain size, so mechanism claims separate from the observation that scaling occurs.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/PatternScaling.lean with Delphi.Pattern.scales_of_expansion_repression and Delphi.Pattern.no_scaling_without_feedback, entering the registry as law_id `pattern-scaling-of-mechanism`
reads: Mathlib analysis lemmas for the gradient length

buildable.why: The steady-state model and its gradient length are already implemented with sourced coefficients, and the scaling statement is a consequence of a stated feedback structure. Large because it needs a formalisation of the dynamics rather than of an algebraic ratio.

gaps.risk: The implemented model is source-sink diffusion, one of two live hypotheses for Fgf8, with gastrula coefficients used for a fin bud. A theorem about that model would inherit all of it, and this repo's own pre-registered test of the model FAILED on the axis that mattered. A law here must be scoped to the model and not to development.

gaps.name: lean_module_wbe_derivation
gaps.need: Whether the three-quarters exponent follows from space-filling, area-preserving branching and size-invariant terminal units, with asymmetric branching as a stated variant.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/Network.lean with Delphi.Network.exponent_of_premises and a variant for asymmetric branching, entering the registry as law_id `wbe-network-exponent` with class theorem-from-hypothesis
reads: lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean for the ratio and log-slope idioms

buildable.why: Mathematically self-contained: the derivation is a consequence of stated geometric premises and needs no data. It is large because the original derivation is informal in places and formalising it means choosing which reading to formalise, which is itself part of the dispute.

gaps.risk: Proving the derivation valid would be reported as confirming three-quarters scaling, which it would not do: real vasculature may not satisfy the premises, and Kolokotrones et al. report the empirical relation is curved, so a single exponent may be the wrong model entirely. Proving it INVALID would be equally over-reported in the other direction.

gaps.name: data_mortality_schedules
gaps.need: Age-specific survival and fecundity schedules for at least one organism, with sources, so an age-specific sensitivity law has a satisfiable instance.
gaps.signature: a sourced schedule table under sim-engine/params/, one row per age class, with the population, conditions and provenance kind per row
reads: no existing repo file: this is an acquisition

buildable.why: Small as an acquisition and still a real blocker: this registry refuses a law with no satisfiable instance, so the Lean module cannot be proposed until at least one schedule is in the repo with a source.
needs_data: an age-specific life table with survival and fecundity, laboratory or field, with the source quoted

gaps.risk: Laboratory schedules differ systematically from field schedules, and the evolutionary theories of ageing are about the latter. A law whose witness is a laboratory table must be scoped to say so.

gaps.name: lean_module_error_threshold
gaps.need: Eigen's error threshold as a proved inequality over stated fidelity, genome length and selective superiority, so a claimed prebiotic genome length can be eliminated against a claimed fidelity.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/ErrorThreshold.lean with Delphi.Eigen.threshold and Delphi.Eigen.length_rules_out, entering the registry as law_id `eigen-error-threshold`
reads: Mathlib real logarithm and power lemmas

buildable.why: A single inequality between three stated quantities, with the elimination form following the pattern already used by a dozen rules_out theorems here. The cheapest high-value formalisation on the list.

gaps.risk: The threshold follows from the quasispecies premises: deterministic dynamics, effectively infinite population, a fixed landscape. Those are strong and the published objections are about exactly them, so the named hypotheses must carry them explicitly or the law will be applied to finite stochastic systems it does not cover.

gaps.name: lean_module_code_optimality
gaps.need: Optimality of the standard genetic code within a STATED space of alternatives under a STATED objective, with both stated as named hypotheses.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/CodeOptimality.lean with Delphi.Code.optimal_in_space and Delphi.Code.claimed_optimality_rules_out, entering the registry as law_id `genetic-code-optimality-in-stated-space`

buildable.why: The standard code is already a total function in Genotype.lean with codon-space distance decided by the kernel, so an objective over assignments is computable and a finite space of alternatives is enumerable. The combinatorics may need care but needs no data.

gaps.risk: An optimality result would be reported as explaining why the code is as it is. Optimality is relative to an objective, the objective is not observable, and all four historical accounts of the code's origin are consistent with the standard code being optimal under some objective. The statement_en must make the relativity to the stated objective unmissable.

gaps.name: lean_module_selection_sensitivity
gaps.need: Age-specific sensitivity of fitness to a change in mortality, from stated survival and fecundity schedules, which is the one piece of ageing theory that is pure arithmetic.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/Senescence.lean with Delphi.Senescence.sensitivity_declines and Delphi.Senescence.claimed_force_rules_out, entering the registry as law_id `selection-sensitivity-with-age`
reads: lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean for the frequency and mean idioms
a schedule dataset (does not exist here)

buildable.why: The mathematics is tractable, but this registry refuses a law with no satisfiable instance, and there is no age-specific survival and fecundity schedule in this repo to build a non-vacuity witness from.
needs_data: age-specific survival and fecundity schedules for at least one organism, with a source

gaps.risk: Proving that selection against late-acting effects is weak would be read as establishing an evolutionary theory of ageing. It establishes an arithmetic consequence of the schedules, and this grand question's honest verdict is that almost all of it is empirical remainder.

gaps.name: data_gp_panel
gaps.need: A combinatorial mutant panel with one consistently measured phenotype, so additivity and epistasis can be tested rather than assumed.
gaps.signature: a sourced dataset of genotype-phenotype pairs over a defined mutational neighbourhood, with the phenotype definition and assay recorded per row
reads: no existing repo file: this is an acquisition

buildable.why: The omics universe here is annotation, not measurement of a phenotype across genotypes. Without such a panel the additive-variance statement and the genotype-network reachability law both lack any instance to be checked against.
needs_data: a combinatorially complete or near-complete mutant set with one phenotype assayed throughout

gaps.risk: A panel measures one phenotype in one background. Conclusions about the genotype-phenotype map drawn from it generalise no further than that, and the provenance kind for using it outside that context is 'borrowed'.

gaps.name: lean_module_flux_feasibility
gaps.need: Whether a stated growth flux is achievable in a stated stoichiometric network, with a kernel-checkable infeasibility certificate rather than a solver's word.
gaps.signature: a Lean module lean/Delphi/Flux.lean with Delphi.Flux.infeasible_of_certificate and Delphi.Flux.claimed_growth_rules_out, entering the registry as law_id `flux-infeasibility-certificate`
reads: a stoichiometric reconstruction (does not exist here)

buildable.why: Checking a Farkas-style infeasibility certificate in Lean is tractable mathematics, but there is no metabolic reconstruction in this repo. The omics universe is 3,860 zebrafish genes with pathway annotation, not a stoichiometric model of anything.
needs_data: a stoichiometric network with bounds, for example the published syn3A reconstruction

gaps.risk: A proved infeasibility is only as good as the reconstruction: one missing reaction makes a feasible network look infeasible, and the proof would be correct and the conclusion wrong. The law must carry the reconstruction's version and its known gaps as named hypotheses.

gaps.name: data_relatedness_eusocial
gaps.need: Within-colony relatedness and measured fitness effects for the clades where eusociality originated, so the empirical half of the Hamilton's-rule dispute has anything to stand on here.
gaps.signature: a sourced dataset of relatedness estimates with the marker set and estimator recorded, paired with measured fitness effects for interacting individuals
reads: published colony genotyping and fitness studies
no existing repo file: this is an acquisition

buildable.why: Nothing in this repo touches social behaviour, relatedness or insects. Acquiring this is a research programme and it is listed so that the formalisable core of the Hamilton's-rule question is not mistaken for the whole of it.
needs_data: within-colony relatedness with the estimator stated, and additivity-tested fitness effects for interacting pairs and for groups

gaps.risk: Relatedness estimates depend on the marker set and the estimator, and the dispute turns in part on which definition of relatedness is in play. A dataset that records a number without its estimator would be worse than no dataset.

not_gaps.name: nanopub signing and publishing
not_gaps.why_not: Deliberately absent, not missing. Signing and publishing a nanopub is irreversible; it is done only by the key owner, with explicit approval and the test registry first. Every draft here is unsigned, carries no human ORCID and no key, and CI refuses a personal identifier in an approval field. A tool for it would be a tool for making that mistake quickly.
not_gaps.owner: the key owner, with explicit human approval

not_gaps.name: flight_sim
not_gaps.why_not: It would wrap the physics simulation's equations, which are not currently exposed as an importable module, and physics/ belongs to another thread. A tool that cannot run is not listed, so tools/list does not advertise it. Asked for through the hub rather than edited here.

not_gaps.name: whole-embryo all-atom simulation
not_gaps.why_not: Not deferred but impossible: many orders of magnitude beyond any available GPU. 'Molecular level' in this engine means molecular species and channel conductances in a cell-based tissue model, not atoms, and CONTRACT.md says so to stop the word being read the other way.

not_gaps.name: a tool that returns a truth value for a claim
not_gaps.why_not: There is no such thing here to return. Belief is an ordering heuristic with unfitted parameters, assessor scores are graded judgements in the unit interval and not probabilities, and a law's status is a decision about review. Each of those is served with its own name precisely so that nothing can be mistaken for a probability that a claim is true.

not_gaps.name: automated acceptance of a law
not_gaps.why_not: propose.mjs stops at `candidate` by design and never returns accepted. Promotion requires a person to set approval.approved_by_role and cut a lawset with release.mjs, which refuses an accepted law without that role and refuses a role that looks like an e-mail address. Automating it would remove the only human check in the chain.
not_gaps.owner: a human project role, never an agent

not_gaps.name: anything about the held-out exam clade
not_gaps.why_not: One clade is frozen as a blind exam. The pipeline withholds every record whose text, claim id or taxon id touches it BEFORE any service call, screens service responses for homonymous genera, reports only the count withheld (69 records), and CI fails if an output names it. A tool to reach it would defeat the exam, and the omission is the point.

not_gaps.name: first-class open questions with Lean-formalised arms
not_gaps.why_not: Being built by another thread under lean/registry/open-questions/ and not duplicated here. This map's open_questions_list gap is the serving layer over the raw enumeration in open-problems/, and when that registry lands the tool should read it instead and treat open-problems/ as the material behind it. Coordinate through the hub.
